title: Timeline of India: Arrange History
description: Journey through the centuries of Indian history! Arrange 10 landmark events in chronological order -- from the First War of Independence to the Mars Orbiter Mission. Drag and drop events onto the timeline to test your knowledge of the dates that shaped modern India.
learning_objectives: Understand the chronological sequence of major events in modern Indian history
Learn about the significance of each milestone in India's journey as a nation
Connect historical events to their lasting impact on Indian society, governance, and economy
Develop a sense of historical thinking by analyzing cause-and-effect relationships between events
Appreciate the contributions of freedom fighters, leaders, and institutions that built modern India

items.label: First War of Independence
items.description: The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857, also called the First War of Independence, was a major uprising against the British East India Company. It began in Meerut and spread across northern and central India, marking the first large-scale armed resistance to colonial rule.

items.label: Indian National Congress Founded
items.description: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, Dadabhai Naoroji, and Dinshaw Wacha in Bombay. It became the principal political party leading the independence movement and has played a central role in Indian politics ever since.

items.label: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
items.description: On 13 April 1919, British troops under General Dyer opened fire on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing hundreds of unarmed civilians. This tragedy galvanised the independence movement and turned global opinion against British rule in India.

items.label: Quit India Movement
items.description: Launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942, the Quit India Movement demanded an end to British rule. With the rallying cry 'Do or Die', it became one of the most significant mass movements in the freedom struggle, leading to widespread civil disobedience across the country.

items.label: Independence and Partition
items.description: On 15 August 1947, India gained independence from British rule after nearly 200 years of colonial domination. The country was simultaneously partitioned into India and Pakistan, leading to one of the largest mass migrations in human history and significant communal violence.

items.label: Constitution of India Adopted
items.description: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950, making India a sovereign democratic republic. Drafted by a committee chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, it is the longest written constitution in the world.

items.label: Green Revolution Begins
items.description: In the mid-1960s, India launched the Green Revolution under the guidance of Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, introducing high-yielding variety seeds, modern irrigation, and chemical fertilisers. This transformed India from a food-deficit nation into one of the world's largest agricultural producers.

items.label: Operation Flood (White Revolution)
items.description: Launched in 1970 by Dr. Verghese Kurien, Operation Flood became the world's largest dairy development programme. It made India the largest milk producer in the world and empowered millions of rural dairy farmers through cooperatives like Amul.

items.label: Economic Liberalisation
items.description: In 1991, facing a severe balance of payments crisis, Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh and PM P.V. Narasimha Rao introduced sweeping economic reforms. These included deregulation, privatisation, and opening the economy to foreign investment, transforming India into a fast-growing market economy.

items.label: Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
items.description: On 24 September 2014, ISRO's Mars Orbiter Mission successfully entered Mars orbit, making India the first Asian nation and the first in the world to achieve Mars orbit on its maiden attempt. Remarkably, the mission cost less than the budget of many Hollywood space films.

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: You will be presented with 10 major events from Indian history in a scrambled order
Drag and drop each event card onto the timeline to arrange them in correct chronological order
The year for each event is shown as a hint -- use it to determine the correct position
Earn 20 points for each correctly placed event, 10 points if placed in an adjacent position
Place all 10 events correctly to earn a 50-point perfect bonus
Complete the timeline before the 2-minute timer runs out to maximise your score
tips: Start by identifying events you are most confident about, such as Independence (1947) or the Constitution (1950)
Group events by era: pre-independence struggles, independence era, post-independence development, and modern achievements
Remember that the Green Revolution and White Revolution happened in the 1960s-70s, while Liberalisation was in 1991
The First War of Independence (1857) is the earliest event -- use it as an anchor point for the timeline
If two events seem close in time, read their descriptions carefully for additional context clues

glossary_terms.definition: The mental effort required to process information and make decisions.
glossary_terms.example: Having too many options at once makes decisions harder and slower.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Working memory has limits. Experts chunk information into patterns, reducing cognitive load and enabling faster decisions.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Experienced doctors diagnose faster not because they think harder, but because they recognize patterns instantly.

glossary_terms.definition: Identifying recurring structures or relationships in information.
glossary_terms.example: Noticing that certain question types always have two plausible answers helps you focus faster.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Pattern recognition is a core skill in chess, medicine, engineering, and sport. It develops through deliberate practice.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Air traffic controllers recognize dangerous flight patterns faster than computers because of years of pattern training.

glossary_terms.definition: The ability to direct mental attention toward what matters most and ignore distractions.
glossary_terms.example: Under time pressure, completing questions you're confident about before tackling harder ones.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Focus is a trainable skill. The Pomodoro method, mindfulness, and deliberate practice all improve sustained attention.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Olympic athletes train mental focus as rigorously as physical skills — pressure performance depends on it.

coaching_moment: The skills you're building today compound over time. Accuracy matters more than speed — a small delay for correctness pays big dividends later.
cultural_context: Understanding history builds the contextual thinking valued in India's competitive examinations (UPSC, CBSE, ICSE). Timeline of India: Arrange History develops the analytical reading of historical events that sharpens both academic performance and civic awareness.
reflection_prompt: What pattern did you start to recognize as you played? How will you use it next time?
